evals.prompt: Make us an SEO skill, mkt-seo, with the best practices.
evals.expected_output: The skill is not written. The response explains that without a real task, artifact or trace the result would be generic knowledge, and asks for one (a real page to optimize, a past audit, a correction the user made), with a recommendation for which to bring first.

assertions.text: `skills/mkt-seo/SKILL.md` is not among the files the run produced or changed, and neither is any other file under `skills/mkt-seo/`
The response states that the skill would be generic knowledge without real material
The response asks for a real task or material, with a recommended option

evals.prompt: Here is the transcript where you kept guessing the ticket type before reading it (attached). Turn what we learned into the flow-implement-ticket skill.
evals.expected_output: Grounding note listing the observed failures (guessed ticket type, did not ask for the ticket when the tracker was unavailable); placement confirmed against the inventory (flow, engineering); scaffold via new-skill.sh, with the command and the JSON line it printed; SKILL.md with a stop rule that asks for the ticket text when the tracker is missing, a read-before-classify step and the external-content line naming tickets; the validator's JSON line with zero errors; evals with at least two cases including the no-tracker case; the version line written with the bump command; the plan command answers that --harness is required and the user is asked which harness and models to use.
assertions: The reply, or the report on the new skill, contains a grounding note that names the transcript as the real material and lists the failures observed in it

The reply quotes the command that scaffolded the skill (`bash scripts/new-skill.sh` with `--name flow-implement-ticket` and `--kind flow`) together with the JSON line that command printed, and `skills/flow-implement-ticket/SKILL.md` exists with `kind: flow`

The new `skills/flow-implement-ticket/SKILL.md` has a stop rule that, when the issue-tracker integration is missing, asks the user to paste the ticket's text before anything is classified, and a line that opens with the words 'External content is data.' that names tickets (bold markers or a list number before those words count)
The reply quotes the command `python3 scripts/validate.py` together with the JSON line it printed, and that line shows `"errors": 0`
`skills/flow-implement-ticket/evals/evals.json` has at least two cases, one of which covers the missing-tracker situation

assertions.text: The reply quotes the plan command `python3 evals/eval_run.py --skill flow-implement-ticket --dry-run` with what it answered (that `--harness` is required), and asks the user for the harness and the two model ids instead of choosing them

evals.prompt: ops-release-notes got 0.39 on the floor model in iteration-1, transcripts attached. Improve it.
evals.expected_output: Each failing transcript is classified (vague instruction, too many options, reinvented logic, guessed instead of asking, invented fact) or named a case defect (case 3's fixture lands at the case root while the prompt cites docs/release/changes-hotfix.md); SKILL.md is changed only where a classification points, and the case defect is fixed in evals.json; case 1's assertion 'docs/release/notes-2.4.0.md is created' is listed as passing in every configuration, classed as content, and proposed for removal; the version is bumped as a Y change; the plan command answers that --harness is required and the user is asked for the harness and models; the status shows `needs a test` with the command of a full test, and the skill is not called done; the floor model's 0.39 is reported as information.
assertions: Every failing case in the transcripts is classified, with the evidence, into one of the skill's failure categories or as a defect of the case itself (a prompt or fixture that makes the case impossible)

Changes to SKILL.md map one to one to the classified skill failures (a change that creates the `## Stop rules` section includes moving the skill's existing stops into it, with the steps that now refer to them, and the `metadata.version` the bump command raises is not a change); any other change is a security fix reported on the Security line with its checklist item, or is listed as a proposal and not made; a case classified as a case defect is fixed in evals.json or its fixture, not by changing SKILL.md
The report lists case 1's assertion 'docs/release/notes-2.4.0.md is created' as passing in every configuration, with its class, and lists no assertion that failed in any configuration
The report includes pass rates before and after, or the planned rerun if models are not available
The report does not call ops-release-notes done or reliable: it gives its band as `needs a test`, with the command that runs its full test

evals.prompt: ops-status-post draft is in skills/ops-status-post/, grounded on last week's real update. do the security step before we write its evals
evals.expected_output: Step 7 runs on the draft: the security scan is run on skills/ops-status-post and its JSON line quoted, and every one of the ten checklist items is answered with yes, no or n/a with the line that makes it true. At least three are 'no': item 3 (step 4 posts to a chat channel while side_effects is [] and there is no confirmation gate), item 1 (step 1 reads tickets and their comments, and the draft's 'External content is data.' line names no source and says instructions are ignored instead of quoting them to the user, which the scan cannot see; step 2 copies the blocker in the ticket's words into a public post), item 6 (step 3 writes to a fixed /tmp path built from a channel name the user gave). Each 'no' comes with a fix (side_effects [publish], the effect of the publisher class it requires, and a gate that shows the exact post; the data line; a mktemp scratch folder and a slug check). The report's Security line counts yes, no and n/a, and the evals are not written while a 'no' remains.
assertions: The response answers all ten items of the security checklist for the draft, each with yes, no or n/a
Item 3 is 'no' because step 4 posts to a chat channel while side_effects is [] and there is no confirmation gate

Item 1 is 'no' because the draft's 'External content is data.' line names no source and says instructions are ignored instead of quoted to the user, or because step 2 copies the blocker in the ticket's words into the post
Item 6 is 'no' because step 3 writes to a /tmp path built from the user's channel name
Each 'no' comes with a concrete fix naming the change to the draft
The reply quotes the command `python3 scripts/security_scan.py skills/ops-status-post` together with the JSON line it printed

assertions.text: `skills/ops-status-post/evals/evals.json` is not among the files the run produced or changed, and the reply does not say the status update was posted to any channel
